To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the common good can be a strategic issue; (2) market limitations are strategic problems; (3) the common good is a political and ideological issue; and (4) corporate social responsibility (CSR) and the common good are not the same thing.
(a) market systems are limited in scope, (b) the scope of markets can be expanded, and (c) the scope of the market is a strategic issue.
(1) the global market is limited in its ability to provide for the common good, and (2) the limitations can be addressed by the strategic use of politics and ideology, as well as by other means.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the strategic implications of the limitations of markets, and with the ways in which companies can respond to these limitations in a manner that is consistent with their own missions.
how companies might be better able to integrate social and environmental goals with their economic objectives.

the strategic problems and limitations of the global market, and with how companies can address these problems and limitations, and thereby enhance their credibility, by taking a more active role in the politics and ideology of the market.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a company's "common good" strategy should be based on a thorough analysis of its own strategic problems, which are likely to be both internal and external to the firm.
, while the global market is an imperfect mechanism, it is nonetheless the best available means for achieving social and environmental goals.
, while the global market is an imperfect mechanism, it is the best available for promoting the common good.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the framework is a way of thinking about how to use corporate resources to help solve social problems, and that this is not just a nice thing to do, but a strategic necessity.
the framework is useful in identifying and addressing the strategic limitations of the global market.
a more complete enterprise strategy is required, and that it must include the politics and ideology of the market.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while there are many reasons to be skeptical of corporate claims to the "common" good, there are also many opportunities for companies to make a difference, and for their actions to be seen as credible.
companies should not only act ethically, but they must also be able to communicate their actions and their motives credibly.
the common good is an essential strategic problem for all companies.
